title: 28.29 · Force between opposite currents
given: Two long wires 0.400 m apart carry 5.00 A rightward and 2.00 A leftward. Consider 1.20 m of each wire.
find: Find the force and whether it attracts; then double both currents.

steps.title: Find the force on either wire

answer: 6.00 µN repulsive; doubled currents give 24.0 µN.
check: Opposite currents repel. The two forces have equal magnitudes and opposite directions.

title: 28.34 · Field from a semicircular wire
given: Current I enters from the left, runs clockwise around an upper semicircle of radius R, then exits rightward along the same diameter line. P is the arc centre.
find: Find B at P, including straight sections.
check: Clockwise current makes B point into the page. This is half the field of a complete loop of the same R and I.

title: 28.40 · Ampère integrals
given: I₁ = 4 A into page, I₂ = 6 A out, I₃ = 2 A out. Counterclockwise paths: a encloses none; b only I₁; c I₁+I₂; d all three.
check: A zero integral does not imply zero field everywhere on the path. Shape and perimeter do not affect this steady-current result.

title: 28.43 · Coaxial cable field
given: Solid conductor radius a and outer tube inner/outer radii b,c carry equal currents I in opposite directions, uniformly distributed.
find: Derive B for a < r < b and r > c.

steps.title: Between the conductors
steps.math: a<r<b:\quad I_{enc}=I\\B(2\pi r)=\mu_0I\quad\Rightarrow\quad B=\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}

check: Between conductors, field is azimuthal with direction from the inner-current right-hand rule. Exterior cancellation depends on equal opposite currents and ideal long coaxial geometry.

title: 28.57 · Where two-wire fields cancel
given: Long wires 0.400 m apart carry 25.0 A and 75.0 A.
find: Find all zero-field locations for same-direction and opposite-direction currents.
answer: Same: 0.100 m between; opposite: 0.200 m outside the 25 A wire.
check: Each solution extends along a line parallel to the wires. There is no cancellation outside for same directions or between for opposite directions.

title: 28.61 · Overhead bus cables
given: Bus input power 65 hp, cable voltage 600 V, separation 0.55 m. Use 1 hp = 746 W.
find: Find current and force per unit length.
answer: 80.8 A; 2.38 × 10⁻³ N/m, repulsive for supply/return cables.
note: The supply and return currents run in opposite directions, so the wires repel. The handout calls this force attractive; its magnitude is the value calculated here.

title: 28.62 · Field on the symmetry axis
given: Wires at (0,+a) and (0,−a) carry equal I, respectively out of and into the page. Observe P = (x,0).
find: Draw each field and net field, derive B(x), graph it, find its maximum and far-field limit.

steps.title: Add the field components
steps.math: r=\sqrt{x^2+a^2},\quad B_{each}=\frac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}\\B_y=0,\quad B_x=2B_{each}\frac ar\\\mathbf B=\frac{\mu_0Ia}{\pi(x^2+a^2)}\mathbf i

steps.title: Find the maximum and far-field limit
steps.math: \frac{dB}{dx}=-\frac{2\mu_0Ia x}{\pi(x^2+a^2)^2}=0\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=0\\B_{max}=\frac{\mu_0I}{\pi a}\\|x|\gg a:\quad B\approx\frac{\mu_0Ia}{\pi x^2}

answer: B = μ₀Ia/[π(x²+a²)] along +x; peak at x = 0; far field ∝ 1/x².
check: The graph is even in x, peaks at zero and falls toward zero on either side. At x > 0 the upper wire field tilts up-right and lower wire field down-right.

title: 28.64 · Force on a loop beside a wire
given: Long wire carries 14.0 A rightward. Loop below it carries 5.00 A clockwise, horizontal length 0.200 m. Top edge is 0.0260 m from wire; bottom edge is 0.100 m from wire.
find: Find net force on the loop.

steps.title: Find the forces on the horizontal sides

note: The two vertical sides have equal and opposite horizontal forces at each height, so those forces cancel.
check: The near edge has current parallel to the wire and is attracted more strongly, so net force is upward toward the wire. The 10.0 cm label is wire-to-bottom distance.

title: 28.65 · Suspended current-carrying wires
given: Two opposite-current wires hang from common supports on 0.0400 m cords, each 6.00° from vertical. Mass per wire length λ = 0.0125 kg/m.

steps.title: Use the free-body diagram
steps.math: T\cos\theta=mg,\quad T\sin\theta=F_B\\\frac{F_B}{\mathcal L}=\lambda g\tan\theta=\frac{\mu_0I^2}{2\pi d}\\I=\sqrt{\frac{2\pi d\lambda g\tan\theta}{\mu_0}}\\=\sqrt{\frac{(8.3623\times10^{-3})(0.0125)(9.80)\tan6.00^\circ}{2\times10^{-7}}}\\I=23.2\ \mathrm A

answer: 23.2 A per wire, in opposite directions.
check: Use the separation of both wires, 2ℓ sinθ, not the displacement of only one.

title: 28.72 · Cancel a loop’s centre field
given: Clockwise circular loop radius R carries I₂. Its centre is distance D above a long horizontal wire carrying I₁.
find: Find I₁ magnitude and direction for zero field at the loop centre.
check: For a rightward wire current the field above it is out of the page. Cancellation is at the centre, not throughout the loop area.
